snippet.title: Nithin Kamath on what makes Zerodha different | The Back Office Ep. 1
snippet.description:
Open a free demat account → https://zerodha.com/open-account/?c=AUOEPP

Over 2 crore Indians invest with Zerodha. Open a free demat account in minutes and invest in stocks, mutual funds, ETFs, and bonds at 0 brokerage. No hidden charges, no gimmicks. Plus, get free access to research tools like Tijori, Sensibull and more.

About the Series!

Welcome to The Back Office!
People know Zerodha. They know the brand, the product, the numbers. What they don't know are the people who built it.

Nithin has done plenty of podcasts and interviews over the years. But most interviewers ask him questions based on what they already know from the outside: the origin story, the flat fee, the bootstrapping narrative. The conversation rarely goes deeper than that. It stays on the surface because the person asking doesn't have enough context to push past it.

And for Kailash, Karthik, and Venu, there are barely any conversations at all. Kailash runs the technology behind every trade on Kite and has 30 people doing what most companies need 300 for. Karthik built Varsity from scratch, a platform millions learn from. Venu holds together the operations and compliance that keep this brokerage alive every single day. The world doesn't know enough about who these people are. 

That's the gap this series is trying to close.

The idea is straightforward. We sit down with members of our leadership team and have honest conversations about who they are, how they think, and what it actually looks like to build and run this company. Not the polished, public-facing version. The real one.

There are a few things we're deliberately staying away from.

It's not a brand exercise. The moment it starts feeling like corporate content, it's failed. It's not hero worship. And it's not a retelling of stories that have already been told elsewhere. If something has been covered on three other podcasts, we don't cover it again, unless we can take it somewhere it's never been before.

We also don't want it to be predictable. The conversations go into how these people actually think about life decisions, the things that worry them, the parts of running a brokerage that the outside world never sees, the relationships within the team, including the disagreements. Some of it will be uncomfortable. That's not a bug, it's the point.

snippet.title: Introducing Kite Screener: Find, track, and trade stocks in one place
snippet.description:
In this video, we walk through Kite Screener, a new tool that lets you filter the market and act on stocks without leaving Kite.

Until now, screening usually happened outside your trading platform. You would scan a list on a screener, check charts and fundamentals elsewhere, then return to Kite to add a stock to your watchlist or place an order. Kite Screener brings all of that into one place. You can choose a stock universe, apply custom filters or ready-made presets, and then review a stock, add it to your watchlist, view charts, create a GTT, or place an order directly from the results.

Kite Screener works across the Nifty 50, Nifty 100, Nifty 500, and Nifty F&O stocks, so you can screen a broad universe or narrow it to just the names you trade. You can filter by market capitalisation, sector, P/E ratio, return on equity, dividend yield, debt-to-equity, and more, or use presets built around price action and fundamentals such as top gainers, 52-week high breakouts, growth stocks, and debt-free compounders.

Whether you are looking for intraday movers, stocks near their 52-week highs, high-volume F&O names, or companies that fit a fundamental filter, the Screener helps you find them and act on them from a single screen.

Learn more about Kite Screener: https://support.zerodha.com/category/trading-and-markets/general-kite/others-kite/articles/kite-screener

snippet.title: How to transfer shares to your Zerodha demat account from any broker
snippet.description:
Learn how to transfer shares from another broker into your Zerodha demat account without selling them, which means no capital gains tax on the transfer.

If your stocks are spread across two or three demat accounts, you can consolidate them in one place. Since a transfer isn't a sale, there's nothing to pay in tax.

There are two ways to do this, depending on whether you want to close your old demat account or keep it:

- Closure cum transfer: close the old account and move your shares to Zerodha as part of the process. SEBI requires brokers to do this for free.

- Off-market transfer: keep the old account and just move the shares. This is done online through CDSL Easiest if your broker is on CDSL, or with a Delivery Instruction Slip (DIS) if they're on NSDL.

For off-market transfers initiated on or after 1 June 2026, Zerodha refunds what your existing broker charges, up to ₹30 per stock and capped at ₹500 in total. This applies whether you're new to Zerodha or a long-time account holder. To claim the refund, raise a support ticket after the transfer, within six months from the transfer date. The refund is credited to your primary bank account. Here's how to claim it: https://support.zerodha.com/category/your-zerodha-account/transfer-of-shares-and-conversion-of-shares/transfer-securities/articles/refund-of-transfer-charges

- Step-by-step guide to transfer shares to your Zerodha demat account: https://support.zerodha.com/category/your-zerodha-account/transfer-of-shares-and-conversion-of-shares/transfer-securities/articles/how-do-i-transfer-shares-from-another-demat-account-to-my-zerodha-demat

snippet.title: What is Dabba trading? Understanding India's underground stock market
snippet.description:
Dabba trading is an unregulated system where trades are recorded privately, in a diary or spreadsheet, but never actually executed on a real exchange.
This video explains what dabba trading is, how it operates outside NSE and BSE, and why it carries serious legal and financial risks for participants in India.

snippet.title: More securities now available for pledging on Zerodha
snippet.description:
Zerodha is expanding the list of securities you can pledge for collateral margin to include securities beyond the exchange-approved list. Here's what's changing and a few important things to note before you pledge.

Many investors and traders hold a mix of stocks, ETFs, bonds, REITs, and InvITs. Earlier, collateral margin on Zerodha was available only against exchange-approved securities, the list the Clearing Corporation permits as collateral. Zerodha is now expanding this list, so you can pledge additional securities outside the approved list and use them as collateral margin for trading.

List of securities eligible for pledging: https://zerodha.com/approved-securities/

In this video, we explain how interoperability between NSE and BSE works, why it was introduced, and what it means for your trades on Kite. 

Learn more - https://support.zerodha.com/category/trading-and-markets/trading-faqs/f-otrading/articles/interoperability-of-exchanges

06:21 - Withdraw to secondary bank accounts

08:51 - Rainmatter ecosystem (https://rainmatter.com/portfolio/)

snippet.title: Your broker doesn't hold your shares. Who does? Depository participant explained
snippet.description:
Most investors assume their stock broker stores their shares. The reality is different, every share you own is held electronically by one of India's two national depositories – NSDL or CDSL. Your broker acts as a Depository Participant (DP), giving you access to your holdings through a demat account.

This video explains the complete journey of your shares – from the moment you click "buy" to how they're stored, transferred, and protected. You'll also learn about common mistakes that can cost you money or create legal problems down the line.

02:53 - What is a depository participant?

snippet.title: What is a Share Buyback? Why companies repurchase their own shares
snippet.description:
In this video, we explain what a share buyback is and why companies repurchase their own shares.

snippet.title: Indians have lost OVER ₹2000 Crores to THIS scam!
snippet.description:
Digital arrests are a rampant form of cybercrime in India, with scammers impersonating law enforcement officers to extort money. 
In the first quarter of 2024 alone, over ₹120 Crores were looted from citizens. 

This video breaks down how these scams operate, the psychological manipulation involved, and the technology used to avoid detection. Learn how to protect yourself from falling victim to these digital dacoits and understand your rights when faced with such threats.
